title: Weather, Climate & Disaster Overlay Library
source_and_design_basis: ENV-04_OVERLAY_MODEL_v1.0.0.json overlay family, relation, intensity, effect-key and deterministic-resolution contract
ENV-05 through ENV-10 preset trait/hint records that deferred weather, hydrology, ecological and geologic conditions
library_rules: An overlay is a reusable environmental delta, never a base environment identity.
No overlay automatically activates another overlay; causal activation remains GM, authored-event, scenario, or separately governed runtime authority.
Relations apply only when both referenced overlays are active in materially overlapping scopes.
ENV-04 intensity bands are semantic unless a source or local profile supplies an explicit mapping.
Semantic deltas do not invent universal movement, damage, endurance, exposure, structural, weather, or disaster formulas.
Stable effect keys deduplicate equivalent contributions while preserving unrelated effects and provenance.
All ENV-11 definitions are owner-authorized content design and do not claim recovered source text.

overlays.name: Heavy Rain
overlays.applicability: Atmosphere or medium capable of liquid precipitation.

overlays.name: Monsoon Regime
overlays.applicability: Active seasonal monsoon regime; permanent climate classification remains preset/local parameterization.

overlays.name: Fog
overlays.applicability: Medium and local conditions capable of ordinary suspended condensate or fog.

overlays.name: Thunderstorm
overlays.applicability: Atmosphere or medium capable of ordinary convective storm behavior; rainfall may be separately represented.

overlays.name: Heavy Snow
overlays.applicability: Conditions capable of frozen precipitation; thermal enabling conditions remain base/local or ENV-12 authority.

overlays.name: Blizzard
overlays.applicability: Snow available for active snowfall or transport plus strong wind; thermal enabling conditions remain external.

overlays.name: Windstorm / Gale
overlays.applicability: Medium capable of significant ordinary wind or atmospheric flow.

overlays.name: Hurricane / Cyclone
overlays.applicability: Ordinary atmosphere and storm context capable of a large rotating cyclone.

overlays.name: Tornado
overlays.applicability: Atmosphere and storm context capable of a localized rotating vortex.

overlays.name: Sandstorm / Dust Storm
overlays.applicability: Loose sand, dust, or particulate material plus sufficient wind; not limited to desert presets.

overlays.name: Hailstorm
overlays.applicability: Atmospheric storm conditions capable of hail formation.

overlays.name: Flood
overlays.applicability: Water source or local condition capable of inundating normally exposed terrain or structures; Floodplain/Flooded Forest identity alone does not activate Flood.

overlays.name: Flash Flood
overlays.applicability: Terrain or drainage capable of rapid concentrated flow.

overlays.name: Drought
overlays.applicability: Sustained water deficit relative to a local baseline; arid presets do not automatically imply Drought.

overlays.name: Storm Surge
overlays.applicability: Coast, shore, estuary, large open-water margin, or other water body capable of wind/pressure-driven level rise.

overlays.name: Tsunami / Seiche
overlays.applicability: Sufficiently large water body and separately established triggering context; ENV-11 does not infer the trigger.

overlays.name: Wildfire
overlays.applicability: Burnable fuel and conditions supporting combustion; vegetation-rich or drought conditions do not automatically activate Wildfire.

overlays.name: Volcanic Ash
overlays.applicability: Airborne ash established near or far from an eruption; active Volcanic Eruption need not remain active.

overlays.name: Volcanic Eruption
overlays.applicability: Separately established active volcanic/geothermal source; a Volcano preset does not automatically imply eruption.

overlays.name: Earthquake
overlays.applicability: Separately established seismic/tectonic or analogous ordinary physical cause; no supernatural cause is inferred.

overlays.name: Avalanche
overlays.applicability: Slope and unstable snow, ice, or debris mantle capable of rapid downslope movement; Highland/Ice Mass alone does not activate Avalanche.

overlays.name: Landslide / Mudslide
overlays.applicability: Slope, bank, cut, fill, or unstable material capable of downslope movement; Heavy Rain/Earthquake may contribute only when separately active.

explicit_non_causation_examples: Heavy Rain does not automatically activate Flood or Flash Flood.
Monsoon Regime does not automatically activate Heavy Rain at every moment.
Thunderstorm does not automatically activate Heavy Rain or Hailstorm.
Hurricane/Cyclone does not automatically activate Storm Surge, Flood, or Tornado.
Drought does not automatically activate Wildfire.
Earthquake does not automatically activate Landslide or Tsunami/Seiche.
Volcanic Eruption does not automatically activate the separate Volcanic Ash overlay.
Blizzard does not automatically activate Avalanche.
